# Exact elimination for the ordinary triangle inverse-chord question

This note treats an ordinary planar triangle and three concurrent caps.
It proves an exact parameterization and eliminates one variable. It does
not prove the proposed inverse-chord lower bound 2/9.

The ordinary target was subsequently proved by a different joint
inequality in
`candidate 919c51f1d263878e`,
Sections 5–7, with the stronger bound 223/1000. The endpoint elimination
below remains valid; its direct endpoint estimate was not needed.

## 1. Scope and canonical coordinates

Let K be a triangle, let the source be an interior point, and let three
nonzero spanning normals v_1,v_2,v_3 sum to zero. Translate the source
to zero. Write q_i for the corresponding captured area divided by |K|,
and sigma_i for the chord length divided by ||v_i||. Define

    lambda_i=(1/sigma_i)/sum_j(1/sigma_j).

The coordinate map x -> (v_1.x,v_2.x) has nonzero determinant and
multiplies all sigma_i by the same absolute determinant. It preserves
the q_i and lambda_i, and makes the normals (1,0),(0,1),(-1,-1).

Assume every cap contains exactly one strict triangle vertex, with the
three vertices distinct, and contains no other boundary vertex. This
incidence conclusion follows in particular from q_i<=128/279 by the
audited theorem `candidate ca9f00bdb64d6d9e`:
128/279<2sqrt(3)-3. Label the captured vertices P_i.

Let a_i=v_i.P_i>0, and let b_ij=-v_i.P_j>0 for i!=j. Since the three
normals sum to zero, a_j=sum_(i!=j)b_ij in each column. Uniformly scale
the coordinates so a_2+a_3=1. Then the data have exactly the form

    a_1=a>0,       a_2=p,       a_3=1-p,       0<p<1,
    b_12=x,        b_13=y,      b_21=z,
    b_31=a-z,      b_32=p-x,    b_23=1-p-y,

where

    0<x<p,          0<y<1-p,          0<z<a.               (1)

The actual vertices are

    P_1=(a,-z), P_2=(-x,p), P_3=(-y,-(1-p-y)).             (2)

Conversely every choice satisfying (1) gives an actual nondegenerate
triangle with zero in its interior and precisely the stated incidence.
Indeed, its three successive origin determinants are

    det(P_1,P_2)=ap-xz>0,
    det(P_2,P_3)=x(1-p-y)+py>0,
    det(P_3,P_1)=yz+a(1-p-y)>0.

They give positive barycentric coordinates of zero. Each vertex has
positive value under its own normal and negative values under the two
others. Thus this is a complete actual geometric parameterization,
not a list of independent cap marginals.

## 2. Exact cap and chord formulas

The cap at vertex i cuts the two incident edges at fractions
a_i/(a_i+b_ij) and a_i/(a_i+b_ik), measured from that vertex. Therefore

    q_1=a^2/[(a+x)(a+y)],
    q_2=p^2/[(p+z)(1-y)],
    q_3=(1-p)^2/[(1-p+a-z)(1-x)].                        (3)

The corner cap has area sigma_i a_i/2. Consequently

    sigma_i=2|K| q_i/a_i,
    lambda_1=(a/q_1)/[a/q_1+p/q_2+(1-p)/q_3].            (4)

These formulas are exact for every choice in (1); no symmetry is used.

## 3. Eliminating z by quadratic intervals

Fix a,p,x,y satisfying their strict conditions in (1), and define

    q=q_1,          C=p^2/(1-y),         D=(1-p)^2/(1-x),
    w=1+a,          v=p+z.

Then

    p<v<p+a,
    q_2=C/v,        q_3=D/(w-v).                         (5)

Let 0<c<1, with the intended value c=128/279. The cap ceiling is
equivalent to q<=c and

    C/c<=v<=w-D/c.                                      (6)

The sorted three-cap profile is

    q_1+q_2+q_3-(3/4)max(q_1,q_2,q_3)<=1.               (7)

Because its left side is the minimum of the three expressions obtained
by quarter-weighting one q_i, (7) is exactly the union of these three
conditions:

    C/v+D/(w-v)       <=1-q/4,
    C/(4v)+D/(w-v)    <=1-q,
    C/v+D/[4(w-v)]    <=1-q.                            (8)

No ordering of the q_i needs to be guessed. Each right side is positive
when q<=c<1. For constants C',D',T>0, the inequality

    C'/v+D'/(w-v)<=T,          0<v<w,

is equivalent to

    T v^2-(Tw+C'-D')v+C'w<=0.                           (9)

It is empty if its discriminant is negative; otherwise it is the
closed interval between the two real roots, intersected with (0,w).
Equations (5), (6), and each of the three explicit intervals (9) give
the exact feasible set for v as a union of at most three intervals.

The part of the inverse-weight denominator contributed by the other
two chords is affine in v:

    J(v)=p v/C+(1-p)(w-v)/D.                             (10)

For any nonempty feasible interval, its supremum is therefore at its
right endpoint if p/C>=(1-p)/D and at its left endpoint otherwise.
If an endpoint is excluded only by the strict inequalities p<v<p+a,
this is a supremum, not an asserted attaining point. The exact formula
(4) consequently eliminates z using at most three explicitly given
algebraic endpoints. This leaves four geometric variables a,p,x,y.

In particular a strict counterexample lambda_1<2/9 exists for these
four fixed variables exactly when an actual feasible interval is
nonempty and its supremum in (10) is strictly larger than

    7a/(2q).                                            (11)

Strictness makes this equivalence valid even if the supremum is at an
excluded geometric endpoint: it is approached by actual interior
points of the nonempty interval. If the interval is a singleton, it
must itself satisfy p<v<p+a to be an actual feasible interval.

This supplies a finite algebraic elimination, but it does not establish
that all of the endpoint values are at most (11). That remaining
inequality is explicitly unproved here.

## 4. Rational bounds for a putative weight at most 2/9

Keep c=128/279. Under the cap ceiling alone, every source barycentric
coordinate alpha_i lies below 1/2. Here is a direct verification. If
alpha_1>=1/2, a one-vertex cap at vertex 2 has edge-intercept parameters
r,s in (0,1) with alpha_1/r+alpha_3/s=1 and area fraction rs. Eliminating
s gives rs=alpha_3 r^2/(r-alpha_1), a decreasing function for r<=1<=2alpha_1.
Thus q_2>=alpha_3/(1-alpha_1). Similarly q_3>=alpha_2/(1-alpha_1), so
q_2+q_3>=1, contrary to q_2,q_3<=c<1/2.

Every corner-cap fraction satisfies q_i>=4alpha_j alpha_k, by the
arithmetic-geometric mean inequality in alpha_j/r+alpha_k/s=1. If z is
the largest source coordinate, then z>=1/3 and z<1/2, and one of the
other two coordinates is at least (1-z)/2. Hence 2z(1-z)<=c. Therefore

    z<=(1-sqrt(1-2c))/2<5/14,

where 1-2c=23/279>4/49. For any two source coordinates, their sum is
greater than 9/14 and each is less than 5/14. Expanding the positive
product (5/14-alpha_j)(5/14-alpha_k) gives
alpha_j alpha_k>5/49. Consequently

    20/49<q_i<=128/279             for every i.            (12)

Suppose also lambda_1<=2/9. Formula (4) and (12) give

    a/q_1 <=(2/7)[p/q_2+(1-p)/q_3]<7/10,
    a<448/1395.                                          (13)

There is also the useful lower bound a>1/5. From the cap ceilings and
(3),

    1+a>=p^2/[c(1-y)]+(1-p)^2/[c(1-x)]
         >=1/[c(2-x-y)].                                 (14)

The first inequality sums the two bounds for p+z and 1-p+a-z; the
second is Cauchy-Schwarz. The first cap ceiling and arithmetic-geometric
mean give

    x+y>=2a(1/sqrt(c)-1).

Thus (1+a)[2-2a(1/sqrt(c)-1)]>=1/c. But sqrt(c)<19/28, so if
0<a<=1/5 the left side is at most (1+a)(2-18a/19), an increasing
function on that interval. Its value at 1/5 is 1032/475, which is
strictly smaller than 1/c=279/128 by 429/60800. This contradiction
proves the lower bound.

Since q_2>=p^2/(p+a), (13) and q_2<=c show p<7/10: at p=7/10 the
quantity p^2-c(p+448/1395) is 167489/7784100>0 and increases thereafter.
The same argument for q_3 gives p>3/10. Finally (14) gives

    x+y<=2-1/[c(1+a)]<82603/235904<9/25.                  (15)

Thus any putative counterexample lies in the explicit bounded region

    1/5<a<448/1395,      3/10<p<7/10,
    x>0, y>0,           x+y<82603/235904,
    p<v<p+a.

These necessary bounds keep the full actual triangle geometry. They
are not asserted to be sufficient, and they do not prove that the
interval test in Section 3 has no counterexample.

## 5. The joint profile cannot be discarded

There is an exact actual triangle with all q_i<128/279 but with
lambda_1<2/9. In (1) take

    a=107/500, p=1/2, x=y=1021/10000, z=107/1000.

Its three vertices are exactly those in (2), and the positivity checks
in Section 1 prove that zero is interior. The cap fractions are

    q_1=4579600/9991921,
    q_2=q_3=2500000/5450253.

Their positive gaps from the ceiling are

    128/279-q_1=1257488/2787745959,
    128/279-q_2=44128/506873529.

The target normalized inverse chord weight is

    lambda_1=249798025/1416152167,
    2/9-lambda_1=584122109/12745369503>0.

Here q_2=q_3>q_1. The joint profile fails by the exact positive amount

    q_1+(5/4)q_2-1=1726234357787/54458497406013.

Thus the individual cap ceiling alone does not imply the proposed
2/9 bound, even for an actual triangle with precisely the required
three-vertex incidence. No mixed-fiber compatibility or criticality is
asserted for this ordinary counterexample.
